process_observations.observation: Three values this build could only mark UNVERIFIED are now proven live, and each one came from the same cited example - the skill's worked report is wrong on reportType and on the owner grouping column, which is a single deepening rather than three.
The list views and the report folder validated against the org untouched, so the rebuild could be confined to one file and the other five verified byte-identical by hash rather than by inspection.

The report still ships without the Escalated criterion its name promises, and after five rejected candidate codes the gap is now a standing post-deploy action rather than something a rebuild can close.

Both declared checkers scored the pre-rebuild report 100 with zero findings while the org rejected it on three separate grounds, so this step's automated gates carry no signal about report correctness at all.

A Report description over 255 characters deploys as valid XML, passes every checker and fails only at the org; the library's DESC rule family covers PermissionSet, Profile, CustomPermission and CustomObject but not Report.

Deploy validation proves a list-view column token is accepted, not that it renders data - a wrong legacy token shows a blank column - so U6 cannot be closed by run 1 and needs a human opening one view per persona.

Dropping PRIORITY from the columns rather than from the groupings was this agent's call: M4-S04's note asks for grouping by Owner then Priority and also lists Priority as a column, and the org allows only one.
The step is rebuilt and its declared tests have not been re-run.
